title: Chicken Parm
subtitle: The hall's Italian night spread

steps.title: Bread the chicken (medium, 15 min)
steps.instruction: Dredge cutlets in flour, egg, then seasoned breadcrumbs. Lay on sheet pans.

steps.title: Bake the chicken (425°F, 18 min)
steps.instruction: Bake until golden and 165°F internal. Top with sauce and mozzarella; broil until bubbly.

steps.title: Cook the pasta (boil, 12 min)
steps.instruction: Boil penne al dente. Toss with warm marinara and hold. Watch color and texture — if it smells sharp or looks pale, give it another minute before moving on.

steps.title: Build Caesar salad (no heat, 10 min)
steps.instruction: Chop romaine, toss with dressing and croutons. Keep cold until serve.

steps.title: Toast garlic bread (425°F, 8 min)
steps.instruction: Split loaves, spread garlic butter, bake until edges are crisp.

steps.title: Plate for the hall (serve)
steps.instruction: Family-style: chicken and pasta center, salad and bread on the sides.

proTips: Hold sauced pasta separate from cutlets so breading stays crisp.
Broil mozzarella only 1–2 min — watch the hall oven.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven for late calls — nothing worse than cold protein after a run.
Taste for salt at the end — hall palates run salty after long shifts.
Pull chicken at 160°F and let carryover hit 165°F — dry breast ruins crew morale.
tonightSpread: Plate Chicken Parm with sides in separate pans so the crew can mix portions.
Line up Chicken Parm on the main counter with serving spoons — firefighters grab fast between calls.
Keep a backup tray warm in the oven at 200°F for late arrivals after a run.
leftovers: Cool leftovers in shallow containers within two hours — deep pots stay hot too long.
Label trays with date and reheat to 165°F minimum before second shift.
Add a splash of stock or water when reheating — thick sauces tighten in the fridge.
whyCrewsLikeIt: The hall's Italian night spread. A hall pick for regular dinner nights — one line, real portions, no drama at the stove.
substitutions: Chicken thighs ↔ breasts (thighs forgive overcooking on the flat-top).
Any short pasta shape works — penne, rigatoni, or spaghetti.
